title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Faith-focused class, with decent Attunement, Strength, and Luck. This makes them well-suited to a Miracle-heavy build, and to using the many Lightning-attuned weapons as they are often also have good Strength-scaling.

While it does indeed have spells, in the form of Heal (which heals) and Force (which throws enemies away from you), it does not have any that causes damage, with the earliest ones not being found until Cathedral of the Deep or Farron Keep. This means the class will have to focus primarily on weapons initially, and will do well to keep them upgraded as offensive Miracles consume a lot of Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This is the only spellcasting-focused starting class in Dark Souls 3 that doesn't have a damage-boosting ring. Presumably this is because the Cleric doesn't have a damaging Miracle equipped from the start, and the Morne's Ring can instead be found in the Road of Sacrifices.
This class has remained remarkably similar throughout the series, always carrying a Mace and the Heal Miracle.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Cleric's Sacred Chime is a fairly good casting tool and is actually the strongest casting tool for Miracles from 45 to 49 Faith. Its Spell Buff (the stat that affects how strong scaling spells are) doesn't actually increase until at least 19 Faith has been reached. Its Weapon Art is Gentle Prayer, a regenerative effect that always restores 360 hp over the course of a minute as long as the Chime is held in an active hand (so replacing it with another item stops it, as does two-handing the item in the other hand). This effect will actually outheal the Heal Miracle by up to 20% until the Chime's Spell Buff reaches 120, and even afterwards it is a strong if slow alternative due to only having about a third the cost in Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Cleric Set is a light, caster-type armor set and as such has low physical defences and high elemental defences, while also having high Poison and Curse resistances.

The first trainer for more Miracles is found in the Undead Settlement for further development.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Mace is an unexpectedly strong weapon for what may at first seem like a spellcasting class, but in reality it is often a **Cleric's** main armament. This is because Strike damage is often the strongest physical damage type as armored and skeletal enemies are weak to it (most other physical damage types have fewer enemies weak to them), strong Strength-scaling for easy damage increases, a fairly good moveset, and has a good Weapon Art for trading hits with opponents. How the Weapon Art works is that Perseverance adds a flat 45% extra absorption and causes the attacks of light weapons to bounce off the user, while also granting great Hyper Armor to prevent being staggered.

The Blue Wooden Shield is not very good, having only decent physical and magic defence with serviceable Stability. While it does have Parry (albeit the inferior Medium Shield version), a strong Weapon Skill shield like the early Silver Eagle Kite Shield would probably serve as a better replacement.

title: Curved Greatswords (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Curved Greatswords (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Curved Greatswords** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

Serving as the intermediate between greatswords and ultra greatswords, curved greatswords are powerful Hyper Armor weapons that boast impressive damage output, with higher Poise health than a greatsword but the same Poise damage as an ultra greatsword. Curved greatswords are renowned for their strong running attacks, though their Slash damage type is more easily resisted by heavy plate armor. Their versatility and attack power make them popular weapons in PvP, though their comparatively slow swing speed can make them difficult to use.

title: Great Hammers (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
However, they are extremely slow to bring to bear, meaning that they must be used with care due to how vulnerable the wielder becomes between attacks. Their extreme weight and immense stamina consumption also means that heavy Endurance and Vitality investment is mandatory, and like other ultra weapons they scale primarily with Strength.

Within the great hammers weapon class, there also exists a sub-class of three **Ultra Great Hammers**, which possess increased Poise health, making them extremely difficult to interrupt once they are in motion. These weapons, Smough's Great Hammer, Morne's Great Hammer and Ledo's Great Hammer, are immensely heavy and require copious amounts of Strength to wield, but when used properly can dominate an area around them, becoming monsters on the battlefield.

Like their smaller cousins, the primary skill used by great hammers is Perseverance, providing instant Hyper Armor to give the wielder increased survivability.

title: Great Hammers (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Great Hammers (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Great Hammers** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

The largest and most powerful class of ultra weapon, great hammers possess the heftiest Poise health and inflict the most Poise damage of all ultra weapons, making them the strongest Hyper Armor weapons in the game. With the exception of the Pickaxe, all great hammers inflict Strike damage, which is the least-resisted physical damage type on the vast majority of all armor, allowing these weapons to inflict much more damage than their peers. Like greataxes, great hammers possess very powerful vertical swings that can stagger foes in an area around the impact point, which can interrupt enemies attempting to outspace the wielder's swings even if they take no damage.

title: Greataxes (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Greataxes (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Greataxes** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

One of the three classes of ultra weapons, greataxes are characterized by their heavy weight, hefty stamina cost and slow swing speed, in exchange for providing strong Hyper Armor and high damage output. Like other ultra weapons, they benefit greatly from investing heavily in Endurance, Vitality and Strength.

Among all ultra weapons, greataxes have a mundane moveset and the least range, but make up for this by inflicting the most damage. As well, like great hammers their vertical swings can inflict stagger on foes in an area around the impact point, making this weapon difficult to space against even by skilled opponents. As the big brother to the axe weapon class, several greataxes also possess the Warcry skill, allowing them to amplify their already high damage output to extreme levels.

title: Halberds (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Halberd movesets are divided into two general categories, those with sweeping weak attacks and those with thrusting weak attacks. However, in practice, only two halberds possess the thrusting moveset, the Halberd and the Red Hilted Halberd. These thrusting halberds have the advantage of attacks that inflict Thrust damage and thus benefit from Counter Attacks, however this is offset by their inability to utilize Hyper Armor with these thrusting attacks.

title: Halberds (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Halberds (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Halberds** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

A special type of polearm, halberds possess sweeping attacks combined with long range to give their attacks strong coverage and reach. With the exception of attacks that perform thrusting attacks, they can also take advantage of Hyper Armor, meaning that Poise will allow them to engage foes inside of the arc of their blades. However, like other polearms, halberds will deal reduced damage to targets that are not hit by the head of the weapon itself.

title: Hammers (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Hammers (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Hammers** are a weapon type in *Dark Souls III*.

Hammers are generally blunt weapons which inflict strike and/or thrust damage, depending on the specific weapon. They are the smallest-sized weapons which have Hyper Armor frames, allowing them to take advantage of Poise, though they are generally only effective at trading against similarly sized weapons. Offensively, they have moderate swing speed and crushing overhead strikes which are powerful for dealing with single targets, and they can deal Poise damage rivaling that of Greatswords. Most Hammers, with the exception of the Drang Hammers, have relatively low Dexterity requirements, making them ideal for Strength builds.

title: Hyper Armor
snippet: Hyper Armor is also activated by some Skills (Stomp being an example), granting more efficiency during the effect. However, opponents may easily avoid the next attack, potentially making the skill useless (especially in PvP).

title: Hyper Armor
snippet:
Hyper Armor -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - premise 
 premise : The inclusion of the Hyper Armor gameplay mechanic has generated some misunderstandings among the gaming community. Most players expected *Dark Souls III* to feature a standard Poise stat, such as that seen in *Dark Souls* and * Dark Souls II*, but Hyper Armor works in a slightly different manner, which lead the community to think that Poise was not even working.

Even if the game creator, Hidetaka Miyazaki, during an interview confirmed that Poise was "working as intended", players who were wearing Heavy Armor sets (such as Havel's Set) noticed they were getting staggered by any kind of attacks, even those from the simplest enemies.

That was until the release of Patch 1.08, which fixed Poise and Hyper Armor functionality.

title: Hyper Armor
snippet:
Hyper Armor -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Hyper Armor** is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Hyper Armor
snippet:
Hyper Armor -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Hyper Armor is a new gameplay mechanic introduced in *Dark Souls III* that applies to the effects of Poise. It activates during the attack animations of the player, allowing them to avoid getting staggered if receiving a hit during this time.

The Hyper Armor's activation depends on three factors:
#The type of weapon wielded by the player.
#The type of weapon wielded by the opponent (either in PvE or PvP).
#The Poise numeric parameter.
This means that "passive poise", as seen in previous installments, does not apply anymore. The player must actually attack or they will get staggered nonetheless. There's an important thing to remember, though: small weapons (such as Daggers, Straight Swords, etc.) don't feature Hyper Armor at all.

title: Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Knight Shield is, along with the Herald's Kite Shield, one of only two starting shields with 100% physical blocking, giving the Knight considerable extra survivability early on. However, its elemental defences are bad and it has somewhat mediocre Stability, making it easier to break that block. It has the Parry, allowing for critical hits if the user knows how to time it properly against enemies.

The Knight Set it is carrying is the strongest starting armor set, with quite good physical defenses and respectable elemental defences, and has a good amount of Poise for if using a weapon or attack capable of activating Hyper Armor. It does however have mediocre status resistances and is fairly heavy, and the Knight largely lacks the ability to exploit its Poise unless a larger weapon is acquired.

title: Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The adequate mental stats mean that just one point in either Intelligence or Faith could let it pick up some helpful spells, Soul Arrow, Spook, and Magic Weapon with the Sorcerer's Staff for the former and Heal Aid with the Talisman for the latter.

Its extremely low Luck of 7, shared with the Pyromancer class, means it is often optimal for a large amount of non-pyromancer, non-luck based builds, due to not wasting any of its starting point in that often sub-optimal stat, though it does lack other classes' starting equipment which might help make them initially more optimal/have earlier access to items for that role.

title: Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Knight** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is the most newcomer friendly-class in Dark Souls 3, thanks to its strong and versatile weapon, its 100%-physical block shield, its strong armor, and its well-rounded stats. It is also suitable to a wide variety of builds thanks to its good Strength and Dexterity, and decent Intelligence and Faith. It also has good Vitality, letting it carry heavier equipment easier.

The Long Sword is a strong and versatile weapon, with fast swings on its light attacks and a strong thrusting attack as its one-handed heavy attack, capable of dealing heavy damage if a Counter Attack is landed. Its Weapon Art, Stance, is similarly versatile, as following as using a light attack while holding the stance leads to a block-breaking uppercut while the heavy attack version is a lunging thrust to catch enemies off guard.

title: Mercenary
snippet:
The starting weapon, the Sellsword Twinblades, is one of the strongest weapons in the game and is capable of inflicting extreme damage when two-handed since it is a Paired Weapon and therefore will attack with both weapons when the block button is pressed. Its Weapon Art, Spin Slash, isn't strong in and of itself but has two strong advantages in that it is unparriable and that a light attack or a block/dual attack combos directly into the Spin Slash and its heavy attack follow up, allowing a devastating combo against lightly armored foes. The Wooden Shield, however, has fallen quite far since its glory days in the previous games due to its poor physical blocking and is mostly only useful for parrying.

The Sellsword Set it wears is decent, having good defences for its weight and being fairly light but has mediocre Poise, though since the class is unlikely to be used for a build using a Hyper Armor-supported weapon (except for maybe the Astora Greatsword) this might not be relevant.

title: Mercenary
snippet:
Mercenary -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Mercenary** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class, with just enough Intelligence to cast several basic Sorceries such as Soul Arrow, Spook, and Magic Weapon, provided a Sorcerer's Staff is bought from the Shrine Handmaid.

title: Mercenary
snippet: The Uchigatana is another strong weapon suitable for this class, and is obtainable early on if a slower Dexterity-based weapon is desired.

title: Plunging attack
snippet:
Plunging attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Plunging attacks have been greatly improved in this game, basically only requiring the player to lock-on to an enemy below, drop down, and press the attack button at any time during the fall, no longer requiring to press it with precision as one gets close to the target. The lock-on system will ensure the player is correctly aligned and positioned toward the enemy while in midair, and the attack will perform as soon as they come in contact with it.

There are plenty of opportunities for using plunging attacks throughout the course of the game, especially if there are large enemies around, like Elder Ghrus or Giant Man Serpents. In these cases, there will usually be structures nearby where the player may lure and perform a plunging attack on them. Message signs can often be found in these areas, where the developers hint the player on performing one of these attacks.

title: Plunging attack
snippet:
Plunging attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - description 
 description : In all three games, the mechanic is basically the same:
#Find a higher spot from where the target is.
#Align the player-character toward the enemy and drop down, making sure to land right next to it.
#Press the attack button ( / ) just as one is about to land.

If the hit is successful, the player will land on the enemy and deal a devastating blow that, in most cases, will kill it, or at least inflict a high amount of damage to bulkier foes.

title: Plunging attack
snippet:
Plunging attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Plunging attacks** are a form of critical attack and a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls*, *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*. It consists in the player's ability to inflict heavy damage on an enemy by dropping from a higher level and landing on them whilst hitting them with their weapon.

title: Plunging attack
snippet:
One of the game's bosses, the Ancient Wyvern, is intended to be defeated precisely by these means, where the player is expected to run through a long gauntlet of enemies and perform a plunging attack at the end to defeat the boss in a single hit.

In addition, some larger enemies, like Great Crabs, Elder Ghrus, and Sulyvahn's Beasts, can be disabled momentarily if the player manages to land on their heads without attacking. If successful, the enemy will get staggered and automatically become open for a riposte.

title: Plunging attack
snippet:
Plunging attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Plunging attacks in *Dark Souls II* require a certain level of precision. The player is required to aim their character correctly toward the enemy and make sure they land right next to it, pressing the attack button as they come close to their target on the way down.

In this game, there are not many instances where plunging attacks can be performed, and due to the level of precision they take, only skilled players are advised to use them in the heat of battle. Certain duel arenas, however, provide structures where this type of attacks can be used against human-controlled opponents in online matches.

title: Plunging attack
snippet: A known—and intended—strategy for dealing with the Taurus Demon in the Undead Burg consists in defeating it via plunging attacks. This is evident by the ladder conveniently put there, which gives access to the top of the tower from where the player just came out. Once at the top, they should not dwindle for too long or the creature will eventually jump up there too. If the player was lucky enough to obtain the Black Knight Sword and invested their souls to properly wield it, the demon will die in a single plunging attack.

title: Plunging attack
snippet:
Plunging attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Most likely, the first opportunity the player will have to have a taste of the plunging attack's power is when fighting the Asylum Demon near the beginning of the game. The player enters the boss arena from a high spot and is expected to initiate the battle with a plunging attack while the demon awaits below. If successful, the boss will sustain a considerable amount of damage and the odds will be balanced a little on the player's favor. Hesitating in starting the battle this way for too long will have the demon making the first move by jumping and bringing the player down to ground level and depriving them the opportunity of gaining the upper hand.

title: Reapers (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Reapers (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Reapers** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

Like halberds, reapers combine the sweeping coverage of a blade weapon with the long reach of a spear, and as such are also subject to the "sweet spot" mechanic that causes attacks that do not connect with the head of the weapon to inflict reduced damage. All reapers deal slash damage, and with the exception of Friede's Great Scythe will inflict Bleed build-up with each attack. Compared to halberds, reapers are characterized by the ability of their attacks to inflict damage through the side of a raised shield.

However, the drawback is that their attacks have no Hyper Armor frames short of their skills. This means that the wielder becomes significantly more vulnerable inside of the arc of the weapon due to lack of Poise, and as such should take care to avoid letting foes get too close.

title: Talismans (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Talismans (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Talismans** are catalysts used to cast Miracles. They are primarily differentiated from the other Miracle catalyst, the Sacred Chime, by the skill Unfaltering Prayer, which grants Hyper Armor frames while casting.

title: Ultra Greatswords (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Ultra Greatswords (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Ultra Greatswords** are a type of weapon in Dark Souls II.

Being among the largest weapons available, this weapon class is sluggish but capable of dishing out copious amounts of damage with each swing. Due to their immense size and weight, it is one of the few classes that can take advantage of hyper armor, meaning that Poise can become a must for these weapons. They also deal very high poise damage, allowing for each hit to stagger almost any enemy. That same weight and bulk is also puts this weapon class at a disadvantage as it means large amounts of stat investment are a must, namely Endurance and Vitality. And its slow swings can, more often than not, leave the wielder vulnerable to counterattacks.

When wielded with two hands, unlike its predecessor, it cannot be parried, with exception of its running and rolling attacks.

title: Ultra Greatswords (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ultra Greatswords (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Ultra Greatswords** are a weapon type in *Dark Souls III*.

Among the largest weapons available, ultra greatswords are very slow but inflict tremendous damage with each swing, and their great length allows them to strike targets from farther away. Their immense weight and bulk allow them to take advantage of Hyper Armor, meaning that Poise becomes a strong advantage when wielding one of these weapons. However, their cumbersome weight and voracious stamina consumption means that heavy investments in Endurance and Vitality are mandatory, and their slow swing speed and long recovery leave the wielder vulnerable in situations where faster weapons would not.

When wielded in both hands, attacks from ultra greatswords cannot be parried, with the exception of running and rolling attacks.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Unusual for a weapon, the Abyss Greatsword has fairly good magic resistance, although most shields are still preferable.

Like Chaos weapons, the Abyss Greatsword scales with Humanity (up to 10). When fully upgraded, with 10 Humanity, and 40/40 in Strength and Dexterity, the Abyss Greatsword deals the most raw physical damage among all of the Greatsword class weapons, beaten only by ultra greatswords and Great Hammers/Axes in this regard. This damage difference is not significant and when factoring in that Abyss Greatsword cannot be buffed, other weapons are capable of vastly out performing this sword without putting points into two different casting stats.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet: If one does not meet the Intelligence and Faith requirements but still meet the required Strength and Dexterity, they will still be able to do full damage with the sword, but, will get a stagger animation that makes them immune to backstabs. This occurs because since the Intelligence and Faith requirements don't actually affect the damage output, but rather the Strength and Dexterity, they can completely disregard investing to get the Intelligence and Faith stats to 18. However, the drawback to this is that it will not allow one to do any follow ups, as once this sword makes contact, it will bounce off, stopping the user from doing anything for a few seconds.

title: Abyss Greatsword
snippet:
Abyss Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Compared to its Greatsword of Artorias' true version, the Abyss Greatsword has a distinct moveset, lower stat requirements, weighs one unit less, has a heavily deteriorated appearance, and deals purely physical damage. The strong attacks are reminiscent of those performed by Artorias himself. Despite requiring 18 Faith and Intelligence, the Abyss Greatsword does not scale off of these parameters. This should discourage most builds from utilizing this weapon.

Unusual for a weapon, the Abyss Greatsword has fairly good magic resistance, although most shields are still preferable.

Swallowed by the Dark with its master, this sword is tainted by the abyss, and now its strength reflects its wielder's humanity.

Alonne Captain Set -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : Although classified as a medium armor set due to its weight, this armor set is in fact designed to be used with the gauntlets and leggings of the Alonne Knight Set, effectively creating a hybrid heavy set.

Compared to the Alonne Knight Set, the supplemented Alonne Captain Set boasts only slightly better physical defenses as well as improved elemental defense, and only an additional point of Poise, at the cost of almost two additional units of weight. However, the defensive differences become much more pronounced as it is upgraded. When all pieces have been upgraded to +10, the Alonne Captain Set provides improved defense against physical and elemental damage across the board compared to the Alonne Knight Set, particularly against slashing damage, although it is still rather weak against lightning damage.

title: Poise (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Poise (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - mechanics 
 mechanics : Poise influences the effectiveness of **Hyper Armor**, which in turn determines whether a player who is in the middle of an attack can be interrupted, or whether the attack continues and hits its target. This is especially important when using powerful but slow weapons such as ultra greatswords. The actual Poise number is expressed as a *percentage* of **Poise Damage** that is reduced when attacked during Hyper Armor frames.

When wielding a weapon capable of utilizing Hyper Armor frames, the player's **Poise Health** is generally determined by the class of the weapon (greatswords, hammers, etc.), though some weapons such as the Greatlance and Crucifix of the Mad King are exceptions that have increased Poise Health. Poise Health is also temporarily increased for the duration of certain weapons' skills.

title: Poise (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Poise (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - increasing_poise 
 increasing_poise : The player's Poise is primarily increased by wearing armor, though it can also be reinforced via the use of three unique pieces of equipment: the Lothric Knight Long Spear, Yhorm's Greatshield and Wolf Ring.

Increasing Poise is subject to diminishing returns, as each individual piece stacks multiplicatively and reduces incoming Poise damage by its listed amount as a percentage (e.g., an armor piece with a Poise value of 8.5 will block 8.5% of incoming Poise damage, causing the attack to inflict 91.5% of its Poise damage). Which again can be further increased via equipping the associated weapons and ring.

title: Poise (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Poise (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - poise_health_modifiers 
 poise_health_modifiers : Poise health during an attack can vary depending on the type of attack.

A weapon uses its base Poise health when performing standard attacks or strong attacks, with certain smaller weapons such as greatswords and hammers being incapable of utilizing Hyper Armor unless two-handed. Performing a running or rolling attack will reduce Poise health to 50% of its base value (and in the case of ultra weapons, allows them to be parried). Performing a fully-charged strong attack, whether one-handed or two-handed, will increase Poise health by 50%.

title: Poise (Dark Souls II)
snippet:

 defense : The player innately has very little poise, which can be increased by leveling the Endurance and Adaptability stats. Players gain Poise via these stats according to the value of the lower one. Poise via leveling increases by 0.3 up until level 30, then by 0.2 up to level 50, then by 0.1 up to level 98, gaining 0.2 at level 99 for a total of 18.

Poise is primarily added by the armor currently equipped, heavier armor typically providing more poise. Poise can also be increased further by using the Ring of Giants, granting 10/20/30 poise at +0/+1/+2.

 poise_damage_modifiers : As with Poise health, Poise damage can also be modified depending on the situation.

A weapon's base Poise damage is considered when performing one-handed standard attacks. When a standard attack is performed while two-handing the weapon, Poise damage is increased by 30%; the same also applies when performing a strong attack while one-handing the weapon. When the weapon is two-handed and a strong attack is performed, Poise damage is increased by 55% of its base value.

title: Poise (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Poise (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - hyper_armor 
 hyper_armor : Hyper Armor is a state a player or NPC can access, usually via specific weapon attacks, which changes how Poise Damage interacts with them.

When Hyper Armor is active, attacks a character receives are altered in two ways:
Hyperstagger gets ignored.
Incoming Poise Damage is reduced.
This way, attacks that can hyper stagger get countered by attacks from heavy weapons and characters that use them can make more use of Poise than characters with lighter weapons can.

Each weapon has a specific Hyper Armor multiplier that corresponds to its weapon class. Weapon class doesn't entirely correlate with the menu 's specified class but rather with the moveset of the weapon.

Not all attacks apply hyper armor, as a general rule it's limited to the slower attacks on weapons.

Dodge rolls have a similar mechanic where they simply ignore poise damage for a section of their animation after their iframes end.

title: Poise (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Poise (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - description 
 description : Poise is the player's resistance to being staggered. Poise works similar to stamina in that it is reduced and refills on its own. Poise is reduced each time the player takes a direct hit. Shields prevent damage to poise when used to block an attack, instead reducing the player's stamina. If poise is reduced to zero the player will become staggered, following which, poise will refill. Poise will otherwise refill at a rate of 0.56 poise per second.

title: Poise (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Poise (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - player_poise_timer 
 player_poise_timer : Each time a hit is taken, poise will reduce and remain briefly frozen at the latest value; it does not regenerate over time. A timer is triggered with each hit that is taken, and if it completes before another hit is taken, poise will instantly refill back to 100%. This means that if a player with 53 poise gets hit by an attack that drains 20 poise, the player will then have exactly 33 poise for the next few seconds. This timer is set to 5 seconds by default and for every piece of poise-granting-armor equipped, the timer's length is reduced by 10%.

title: Poise (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
When the player is hit by attacks while in Hyper Armor frames, they will incur Poise Damage, depending on the type of weapon and specific attack. Whether or not they will be knocked out of the attack is determined by whether the **Stagger Point** is reached, by reducing Poise Health to 0:

If Poise Health is reduced to 0, whether from a single strong attack or multiple weak attacks, the attack will be interrupted and the player will be staggered.

Poise health will be reset to full under the following conditions:
Once the player has been staggered
If the player takes no Poise damage for 30 seconds
Using a skill (certain skills will only restore Poise health back to a maximum of 80%)

If an attack is performed while the player has depleted but not empty Poise health (e.g., it has been reduced during a successfully completed attack), their Poise health will be set to 80% of its maximum at the start of Hyper Armor frames of the new attack.

title: Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls III)
snippet:

 characteristics : Heavy armor sets provide the strongest defenses and the most Poise. However, they are also extremely costly in weight, meaning that the wearer must invest heavily in Vitality if they intend to use heavy armor.

Because of the high absorption values and the great amount of Poise provided, heavy armor is ideal protection for players who intend to equip ultra weapons and perform Hyper Armor trades with opponents. Ultra weapons tend to weigh a lot and cost tremendous amounts of stamina to swing, so equipment such as Havel's Ring and Chloranthy Ring tend to go hand-in-hand with such builds.

Because virtually all heavy sets are plate metal-based, most sets in this category tend to be weak to Strike damage and Lightning attacks, though exceptions do exist. Their plate metal nature, however, also tends to make them highly resistant to Slash damage and Bleed buildup.

title: Attack Rating
snippet:
Attack Rating -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : Attack Rating is one of the main factors that determines how much damage weapons do throughout the Dark Souls series.

Attack Rating, commonly abbreviated as AR is a number specific to each Weapon and each element that depends on the weapon, upgrade level, player stats and other equipment that can affect it. This number is used during each attack through a damage formula specific to each game to determine the damage.

title: Backstep
snippet:
During the backstep, from frame 11 to 14, the player has hyperarmor, i.e. infinite poise. That means, no matter what hits the player, they will not stumble and stay on their feet. For example, the player can backstep through the boulders in Sen's Fortress without being knocked down. Keep in mind that you will still take damage, since the hyperarmor frames do not grant invincibility. The backwards ninja flip does not have hyperarmor frames.
When inputing an attack directly after the backstep, the player will perform a running attack. This can be very useful in combat, by dodging an enemy's attack with the backstep, then striking back with a running attack.

snippet:
Vitality (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Vitality** is one of the eight base stats in *Dark Souls* that can be increased when leveling up. Investing in vitality increases the player's maximum health points (HP).

Contrary to the vitality stats in *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*, vitality in *Dark Souls* does not affect the player's maximum equipment load. In *Dark Souls*, equipment load is governed by endurance.

title: Gauntlets
snippet:
Gauntlets -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : Gauntlets have by far the shortest range of all the weapon types in *Dark Souls*, which means they require getting up close and personal with the enemy. They make up for their limited range with their speed. They can attack extremely fast, being able to create long chains of relentless attacks as long as the player's stamina holds out. Gauntlets are one of the few weapon classes that have the ability to parry when used in the left hand.

With a gauntlet weapon (including fists) equipped in the right hand, the kick animation is changed - rather than a heel kick, the character strikes with the knee. This does not seem to affect the function or range of the kick.

 lead : **Stamina** is a character stat in *Dark Souls* that affects how long and frequently physical actions, such as attacking, blocking, and dashing, can be performed. title: Clawed Curse
snippet:
Clawed Curse -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : Grand Archives Scholars have their own heads covered in wax to protect themselves from these specters. They tend the many vats filled with this liquid found throughout the library.
In the official guide, there is a description for the Scholar's Shed Skin telling how "ivory wax" is made to prevent your "anchor of reason" from being damaged by the "foulness" of the texts. How this works in relation to the curse effect they give is not clear, but they could represent how the mind interprets the harm they do, though how exactly this harms people is uncertain.
They share a resemblance with the arm that appears out of the Curse-rotted Greatwood in its second phase.

title: Bleed (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bleed (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - bleed_attack_bonus 
 bleed_attack_bonus : The Bleed Attack Bonus (abbreviated as Bleed BNS in-game) increases the amount of Bleed buildup inflicted per hit. It does not affect the total amount of damage the Bleed effect will do. Unlike weapons that have a magical scaling stat, Bleed has no equivalent scaling.

The Bleed BNS value is determined by the Dexterity and Faith stats. In order to continually increase innate Bleed BNS, both Dexterity and Faith need to be leveled up, with Dexterity giving a larger bonus.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Parameter Bonus** (also known as **Scaling**) is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls II* similar to the ones from the first game.

It is a rating ranging from "E" to "S" of how well a weapon synergizes with a specific stat. These stats include Strength, Dexterity, Magic (mainly Intelligence), Lightning (mainly Faith), Fire (mainly a combination of Intelligence and Faith) and Dark (lowest stat between Intelligence and Faith).

All the details are not completely known; in particular, how scaling works when there are multiple stats at once (such as for "quality" weapons).

title: Greatsword of the Forlorn
snippet:
Greatsword of the Forlorn -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Greatsword of the Forlorn is a very potent weapon, with the ability to deal massive damage in three different ways.

The weapon deals a great deal of both physical and Dark damage, as well as a good amount of Bleed build-up. This makes the weapon useful against most foes.

The weapon's main mechanic is that it, similarly to the Dark Pyromancy Flame and the Scythe of the Forlorn, scales with how hollow the player is. In human form, it will have an extremely low attack rating, while it will have a slightly above-average damage output when fully hollowed.

Its moveset is similar to that of the Charred Loyce Greatsword; however, two-handed light attacks are standard greatsword swings.

title: Durability
snippet:
Durability -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_equipment_loses_durability 
 how_equipment_loses_durability : Equipment can lose durability in a few ways. Armor, for example, is damaged any time you take damage. Some enemies, such as the Gaping Dragon, Chaos Eaters and Burrowing Rockworms have attacks which decrease the durability of all your equipment. There is also the spell Acid Surge which degrades equipment in the same way as the Chaos Eaters' attacks.

Weapons can lose durability by hitting enemies, walls or breakable objects. Attacks that are deflected, such as when striking a wall, suffer double the durability damage.

 how_to_join : The emblem to join the covenant can be found in the Undead Settlement, inside the leftmost house from the big open area with several peasants and an Evangelist praying at a burning tree.

Upon entering the house, head right and drop through a hole in the floor. The hole is partially concealed by several boxes and dead Cage Spiders. The covenant item is on a table along a wall opposite a fireplace with a cauldron of Estus Soup.
